newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican stocks close up on hopes for rate fall.
newsitem.headline: Mexican stocks close up on hopes for rate fall.

text.p: Mexican stocks ended the week with gains on Friday, buoyed by a bullish day on U.S. markets and hopes local interest rates will fall next week.
"Money market paper was in great demand, so primary rates are expected to fall by up to 200 basis points next week," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC index closed 34.21 points up, or 1.04 percent, at 3,340.93.
Traders said that falling U.S. long bond rates came as a relief to local markets. Secondary interest rates fell and the peso rallied against the dollar.
Mexico's spot, or 48-hour, peso closed 5.5 centavos stronger at 7.556/7.56 per dollar.

U.S. payrolls and jobless data were well received by local traders and were absorbed well by an oversold Treasury market. Yields on the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond stood at 7.11 percent as the stock market closed, down from an early peak of 7.24 percent.
The Dow Jones meanwhile closed 52.90 points up, or 0.94 percent, at 5,659.86.
"Both domestic and foreign investors were buying but volume was thin," said a trader at the Banorte brokerage.
Domestic and foreign investors entering the secondary money market pushed overnight Cetes rates down 65 basis points at the close to 23.15 percent.
Brokers, meanwhile, said the felt that the bellwether 28-day Cetes rate, currently 25.47 percent, may fall by 150-200 basis points at next week's primary auction.

A total of 103 stocks changed hands, and winners outnumbered losers by 59 to 22. The winners list was headed by holding company Desc C series, which closed up 4.82 percent. Its ADRs closed 7/8 up to 21-7/8.
Retail stock Salinas y Rocha lost most, with its series L shares closing 21.67 percent.
Market heavyweight Telmex closed flat at 12.48 pesos in Mexico, while its ADRs closed 3/8 up at $33 in New York.
-- Mara Luisa Aguilar, Mexico City newsroom 525 7289565
